headline: Day Use Access to the Famous Singing Sands
reservation: Basin Head is primarily a day-use park; no permit is currently required for beach access, though fees may apply for the on-site Fisheries Museum. Accommodation must be booked in nearby Souris or eastern PEI as there is no camping within the park. Check the official PEI Parks site for any seasonal changes to facility access.

days.title: Singing Sands and Coastal Heritage

stops.name: Basin Head Beach
stops.detail: Experience the 'Singing Sands,' where high silica content creates a unique sound underfoot while walking near the tide line.

stops.name: Basin Head Fisheries Museum
stops.detail: Learn about the history of the inshore fishery and the coastal ecology of the Northumberland Strait.

days.driving: Allow 15 minutes from Souris; coastal roads are well-maintained but narrow.
days.note: The 'singing' effect is most prominent on dry sand found further up the beach.

days.title: Points East Coastal Drive

stops.name: East Point Lighthouse
stops.detail: Visit the 'Meeting of the Tides' where the St. Lawrence and Northumberland Strait currents collide.

stops.name: Elmira Railway Museum
stops.detail: Explore the eastern terminus of the Prince Edward Island Railway, now the start of the Confederation Trail.

days.driving: Allow 45 minutes for a relaxed coastal loop; conditions vary with wind.
days.note: Check lighthouse climbing hours as they may differ from general grounds access.

days.title: The Run and Rural Vistas
days.start: Suggested: 11 AM from the Museum Parking

stops.name: The Run
stops.detail: Observe the channel that divides the beach and allows the basin to drain into the sea, a popular spot for local swimming.

stops.name: Red Point Provincial Park
stops.detail: Short drive to nearby cliffs to see the contrasting red sandstone formations characteristic of the island.

days.driving: Allow 20 minutes for local transfers between coastal park sites.
days.note: Swimming in 'The Run' involves strong currents; follow all posted safety signs and lifeguard instructions.

intel.title: Day Use Facilities
intel.text: The beach and park facilities are seasonal, typically fully operational from mid-June through Labor Day. Outside of this window, washrooms and the museum may be closed.

intel.title: Main Beach Lot
intel.text: A large paved lot serves the beach and museum, but it can reach capacity during peak July heatwaves. Arrive early or late afternoon to avoid the busiest mid-day period.

intel.title: Coastal Connectivity
intel.text: Cellular reception is generally excellent across the flat coastal terrain of eastern PEI. Signal may weaken slightly inside the museum's historic structures.

intel.title: Souris Gateway
intel.text: The town of Souris is the nearest hub for fuel, hardware, and groceries. It also serves as the ferry terminal for the Magdalen Islands.

intel.title: Tidal Influence
intel.text: While the beach is expansive at all times, low tide reveals more of the 'Singing Sands' area. Check local tide tables for the Souris/East Point region.

plan.arrival: Fly into Charlottetown (YYG), pick up a rental car, and drive approximately 90 minutes east through rural farmland to the town of Souris.
plan.vehicle: Standard vehicles are ideal for the paved Points East Coastal Drive; larger RVs should be mindful of smaller seaside parking lot turnarounds.
plan.goldenHour: East Point Lighthouse offers an unobstructed horizon for sunrise, while the Basin Head dunes catch the soft evening light looking westward.
